blocks.text: Surrey Farms: what the ground is and what governs it

items.t: Municipality: City of Surrey, BC, whose City-published communities are City Centre, Cloverdale, Fleetwood, Guildford, Newton, South Surrey and Whalley.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect acreage buyers

items.t: City frame: OCP = Surrey 2050 OCP Bylaw No. 21900 (adopted Jun 15, 2026) — never 18020 as current; Zoning Bylaw No. 12000. Servicing: Subdivision and Development Bylaw No. 8830 (1986), verified on the City's own pages — for an ALR parcel, ALC approval is required in addition.

Suites / SSMUH: Surrey's urban suite rule is one secondary suite per single-family, semi-detached or duplex dwelling unit, at most 40% of the principal unit's habitable floor area, never inside a coach house or garden suite and not a separate strata lot. Surrey's SSMUH framework — a maximum of 3 units on lots smaller than 280 m², 4 units on lots larger than 280 m², up to 6 units on eligible lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent bus stop — applies, on the City's own statement, to eligible residential lots under 4,050 m² within the Urban Containment Boundary, with exemptions including certain hazard lands and properties not connected to community water and sewer. SSMUH is an urban-lot framework; it is not a route to extra dwellings on ALR farm parcels, where the ALC rules above govern.

Creek-side farm ground in South Newton carries riparian rules the listing will not headline: The South Newton plan area includes fish-bearing creeks — Archibald Creek headwaters, Sullivan Heights Creek and Hyland Creek tributaries — and Surrey's streamside setbacks run by stream class in Part 7A of Zoning Bylaw 12000.

The replacement-house trap is the quietest ALR cost: Living in the existing house while building its replacement needs ALC approval; the no-approval route is demolish-and-remove first. A buyer who prices a farm purchase on "live in the old house during the build" without that approval has priced a plan the rules do not give by right.

Surrey farm land is the lowland ring around the urban core, not one district: about one-third of the city is designated Agriculture in the Official Community Plan (OCP), and 95 percent of that land is in the Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR).
Farm Surrey is in the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board (FVREB) area; the board's own community list for its members is Surrey, Langley, White Rock, North Delta, Abbotsford and Mission.

The farm dwelling pattern is one principal house on a large parcel, sited on a limited farm residential footprint at the front of the lot: a City report for 17023 88 Avenue in Cloverdale describes a 1.98 hectare A-1 (General Agriculture) lot farmed with cedar trees on about 0.48 hectares, with the house siting rules meant to preserve the farmed area behind it.

The 4947 192 Street property is 16.1 hectares, of which 12 hectares are used by a golf driving range and mini-golf operation that the Agricultural Land Reserve Use Regulation treats as a non-farm use — an example of the non-farm uses that sit inside Surrey's farm belt under Agricultural Land Commission (ALC) permission.

A second, smaller dwelling for farm help is the other recurring farm-house form: a City committee summary for 17139 40 Avenue describes a new principal dwelling plus an additional dwelling unit under 90 square metres for farm help on a 3.8 hectare property with farm status, used for hay production.

blocks.text: Surrey Farms: rules that affect buyers

items.t: One principal residence per ALR parcel is the general rule: the ALC states that land in the ALR may have no more than one residence per parcel unless the owner qualifies for an additional residence, and a local government may regulate or restrict residences further through zoning.

The principal residence size limit is 500 square metres of total floor area, with no more than 1,000 square metres of fill placed for its construction; a larger residence needs ALC approval through a non-adhering residential use application.

A secondary suite is permitted in the ALR only inside the principal residence: the ALC requires the suite to be entirely contained within the principal residence, a detached dwelling cannot be used as a secondary suite, and local bylaws must also permit it.

Subdivision in the ALR needs ALC approval as a rule: the ALC's Information Bulletin 09 covers subdivision and plans that cause subdivision in the ALR, and the permitted subdivisions an approving officer can approve without a Commission application are narrow — consolidations, boundary adjustments with no parcel under 1 hectare and no increase in parcel count, and similar cases.
Surrey's own ALR exclusion policy is Policy No. O-51: the City planning report on its agriculture policies names O-51 alongside ALC approval as governing non-farm uses and exclusions on A-1 land.

blocks.text: Surrey Farms: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The Surrey Dyking District dates to 1910: the City records that farmers began reclaiming the lowlands with dykes and canals in the late 1800s and that the Surrey Dyking District was formed in 1910 under the Drainage, Ditch, and Dike Act to build sea dams on both the Serpentine and Nicomekl Rivers.

The coastal floodplain holds over 60 square kilometres of agricultural land and over $100 million in annual farm gate revenue, per the City's coastal floodplain page — the scale behind Surrey's drainage parcel charges and flood work.

A farm home plate has a depth limit in A-1 practice: the City's report for 17023 88 Avenue describes the maximum depth of the farm residential footprint and of a single-family dwelling as intended to preserve agricultural land, and the application needed a rezoning to a Comprehensive Development zone to relax farm homeplate and dwelling setbacks.

Fill is regulated on a farm house site: the ALC caps fill for a principal residence at 1,000 square metres including structural aggregate for foundations and driveways, and fill beyond that requires ALC authorization through its notice-of-intent or soil-or-fill application process.

blocks.text: Surrey Farms: development and new projects

items.t: Nicomekl River dike rehabilitation — replacement of three culvert sets plus dike raising protecting more than 50 buildings including homes and barns, over 400 hectares of agricultural land, and parts of 48 Avenue and 184 Street; status: scheduled for completion summer 2027, provincial release (as of November 3, 2026).

4947 192 Street (Cloverdale) — rezoning from A-1 to Comprehensive Development based on A-1 to formalize an existing golf driving range and mini-golf operation permitted conditionally by ALC Resolution #442/2021; status: planning report dated July 27, 2026 (as of November 3, 2026).

Drainage parcel tax for Class 1 (residential) property in Surrey is $250.71 for 2026, collected with the tax notice — farm parcels carrying a residential class component meet this charge alongside the $300.00 Capital Parcel Tax.

Farm classification changes the assessed value the tax is applied to: BC Assessment states the Classification of Land as a Farm Regulation sets income thresholds a producing farm must meet to obtain and keep farm class, and that BC Assessment must confirm a farm continues to meet them, because farm class brings regulated land rates and lower assessed values.

Farm Surrey is road country: Highway 15 (176 Street, Pacific Highway) runs through the Cloverdale farm blocks to the Pacific Highway border crossing, and Highway 99 runs through South Surrey past the Hazelmere farm area to the Peace Arch crossing, as the City's community descriptions note for South Surrey's two border crossings.

Colebrook Road and King George Boulevard are the lowland farm connectors across the Serpentine and Nicomekl floodplain between Newton, Cloverdale and Mud Bay — the same corridors the City's flood pages name for high-tide and dike work, so a farm viewing after a storm should check road conditions first.

blocks.text: Surrey Farms: risks and due diligence

items.t: Confirm ALR status parcel by parcel before anything else: the ALC's housing page states the one-residence rule and size limits apply to land in the ALR, and local zoning can be stricter — a Surrey farm buyer needs both the ALC position and the A-1 zone position for the specific parcel.

Check the floodplain layer for any lowland parcel: the City states most of Surrey's floodplain is protected by dykes, that sea dams on the Nicomekl and Serpentine were first built in 1912 and 1913, and that spillway cells are typically located on agricultural fields — a field can be a designed flood-holding area, which the listing will not say.

Check for existing non-farm uses and their ALC decisions before buying a farm with a business on it: the 4947 192 Street range operates under ALC Resolution #442/2021 and a historic restrictive covenant prohibiting new golf facility structures or expansion, per the City report — permissions can be conditional and time-limited.

Soil and fill history matters in the ALR: the ALC regulates fill placement for a principal residence above 1,000 square metres of fill area, so a parcel with extensive placed fill may carry an unauthorized-fill issue the buyer inherits.

faq.a: On ALR land, one additional detached residence is permitted without an ALC application where the conditions are met — 90 m² or less on parcels of 40 ha or smaller, 186 m² or less on larger parcels — and City of Surrey bylaws must also permit it; anything beyond that requires an ALC application showing the residence is necessary for farm use.
faq.q: Can a Surrey farm have a second dwelling?

faq.a: That replacement-house route needs ALC approval; demolishing and removing the old residence first is the route that does not. Price the plan accordingly.
faq.q: I want to live in the old house while I build the new one — allowed?

faq.a: Only up to a limit without applying. The Agricultural Land Commission permits one principal residence of 500 square metres or less of total floor area per ALR parcel, with no more than 1,000 square metres of fill placed to build it. Anything larger needs a non-adhering residential use application, which the Commission can approve only on its own criteria, and Surrey's A-1 zoning and farm residential footprint rules apply on top of the provincial limit.
faq.q: Can I build a large house on a Surrey farm parcel?

faq.a: More than that needs Commission approval and must be necessary for farm use.
faq.q: Can I add a second house for family or farm help?

faq.a: Not as of right. Subdivision of ALR land is an Agricultural Land Commission matter, and the Commission's Information Bulletin 09 limits the subdivisions an approving officer can approve without an application to cases such as consolidations and boundary adjustments that create no new parcels and leave no parcel under 1 hectare. A plan to split a farm for residential lots is an application with no guaranteed outcome, not a zoning entitlement.
faq.q: Can I subdivide a Surrey farm into smaller lots?

faq.a: Land can be in the Agricultural Land Reserve and still not hold farm class if the income and production requirements are not met.
faq.q: Does buying ALR land automatically give me farm tax class?
